findings.target: Pinned tests/vendor/execution.py run_process timeout cleanup, inherited by controller
findings.observation: On timeout it sends SIGTERM to the group and escalates only if p.wait(timeout=3) still waits for the leader. If leader exits while descendant survives SIGTERM, no group SIGKILL occurs.
findings.effect: Controller can record a finished timeout while a descendant remains alive; violates stated whole-process-group cleanup and can overlap later host work.
findings.reproduction: evidence/INDEPENDENT_WATCHDOG_DESCENDANT_PROBE.json: NONPHYSICAL parent exits on TERM, child ignores TERM; parent receipt timed_out=true/returncode=-15 at 0.302764505999221 s; child alive after return, then explicitly cleaned.
findings.minimal_correction: Use an additive corrected watchdog for this controller, retaining original execution bytes. Escalate remaining group independently of leader liveness, reap the leader, preserve actual cleanup/timeout receipts. Validate one parent-exits/child-survives probe.
findings.resolution: Additive controller-local run_process_group now sends residual-group SIGKILL after every timeout independently of leader exit, reaps the leader, and also cleans its new group on exceptions. Pinned historical execution.py remains unchanged.

notes: Visible runner scanning does not establish absence of previously orphaned native children; actual NCP intake should examine host jobs/processes as already required.
This review preserves scientific definitions/tolerances and makes no change to existing physical evidence.
